simplicity_assessment: No circuit parts, rails, firmware, user interfaces, layers or purchased connectors were added for routing. Two-layer construction and direct soldered wire pads retain the accepted manual-prototype process.

The two PhotoMOS channels and existing discharge/connection/overvoltage components implement the approved fault-handling architecture. Removing one to reduce BOM would be a circuit/function change requiring new electrical/fault evidence and input approval, not a justified routing simplification.

The10thermalvias and clipped front/back DC_RETURN areas implement the declared thermal experiment without adding heatsink hardware, layers or a broad switched-node plane. Their geometry is not proof of the85K/W target.

140x100mm is the accepted independent laboratory footprint. Shrinking it to bulb size now would invalidate placement/spacing/thermal access; no current-stage requirement or verified compact substitute supports that change.

C5 legacy-series procurement risk remains explicitly open before assembly. Similar footprint is not adequate grounds for an unapproved MPN substitution. Bare-board routing can be reviewed without pretending assembly parts have been procured.
